Source: {{SITE_URL}}/about

About

# About ASSOCADS

ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science, is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026. It aims to build a collaborative ecosystem that connects students, professionals, academia, industry, startups and government in AI, Data Science and Analytics across India, beginning with West Bengal.

Why it exists

## One shared home for AI and Data Science

Work in AI, Data Science and Analytics happens in many places at once: in classrooms and research labs, in companies and startups, and in government departments. ASSOCADS was set up to connect them, so that students, professionals, academics, entrepreneurs, investors, institutions and government can learn, meet, research and build together.

It is a not-for-profit public charitable trust. It is non-political, non-religious and open to everyone without discrimination, and its assets can never be shared among its trustees or members.

Who started it

## Founded in Kolkata

Meet the trustees

ASSOCADS was started in 2026 by professionals in AI, Data Science and Analytics. Its first Board of Trustees has seven Founder Trustees, and five founder members work with them on its sub-committees.

Trustees serve without payment. The Board has elected its office bearers, including a President, a General Secretary and a Treasurer.

Vision

## An ecosystem enabler, and in time an apex professional body

ASSOCADS aims to connect talent, knowledge, innovation and opportunity. In the long term, it aims to grow into an apex professional body for AI and Data Science.

Scope

## Across India, beginning with West Bengal

ASSOCADS aims to build a collaborative ecosystem for AI, Data Science and Analytics professionals across India, beginning with West Bengal, and to connect industry, academia, startups, government and society.

Where we sit

## How ASSOCADS is different

ASSOCADS is a public charitable trust open to individuals and broad by design, which sets it apart from trade bodies, certification providers and single-field societies.

How ASSOCADS compares with other kinds of organisation in the field
| Question | Others in the field | ASSOCADS |

| Who can join | Others in the fieldIndustry trade bodies count companies as their members. | ASSOCADSA public charitable trust whose membership, once open, is meant for individuals, including students, as well as organisations. |

| What it is | Others in the fieldCommercial certification providers sell credentials. | ASSOCADSA public charitable trust with named trustees, governed by a trust deed and run for public benefit. |

| What it covers | Others in the fieldSome societies focus on one field or one conference. | ASSOCADSAI, Data Science and Analytics across academia, industry, startups and government: membership, training, research, startups, policy and social good. |

Read our approachRead our aims and objects

Questions

## Common questions

All questions

**What is ASSOCADS?**

ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science, is a not-for-profit public charitable trust set up in Kolkata in 2026. It aims to build a collaborative ecosystem for AI, Data Science and Analytics across India, beginning with West Bengal, that connects students, professionals, academia, industry, startups, government and society.

**Is ASSOCADS registered?**

ASSOCADS is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026. Its registration is in progress.

**Is ASSOCADS affiliated with ADaSci, the Artificial Intelligence Association of India, the Analytics Society of India, NASSCOM, IAMAI or DSCI?**

No. ASSOCADS is an independent public charitable trust. It is not affiliated with, and does not speak for, the Association of Data Scientists (ADaSci), the Artificial Intelligence Association of India, the Analytics Society of India, NASSCOM, IAMAI or the Data Security Council of India (DSCI). It has no partners, members or supporters among these organisations, and their names appear here only to avoid confusion.

**How is ASSOCADS different from industry bodies such as NASSCOM and IAMAI?**

NASSCOM and IAMAI are industry bodies whose members are companies. ASSOCADS is a public charitable trust governed by a trust deed, and its membership, which opens after registration, is for individuals, including students, as well as institutions and companies. Its work covers training, research, responsible AI, startups, policy and social good across academia, industry and government.

About

# ASSOCADS at a glance

ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science, is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026. This page sets out short, dated facts about its legal status, location, trustees and plans, and the organisations it is not connected with, each written to be quoted on its own.

Last updated 24 November 2026

Full name: The full name of ASSOCADS is the Association for AI and Data Science.

Short name: ASSOCADS, always written in capital letters.

What it is: ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science, is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026.

Legal form: ASSOCADS is a public charitable trust. It is non-political, non-religious, not-for-profit and irrevocable.

Legal status: ASSOCADS is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026. Its registration is in progress.

Founded: ASSOCADS was established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026.

Scope: Across India, beginning with West Bengal. It aims to build a collaborative ecosystem that connects students, professionals, academia, industry, startups and government in AI, Data Science and Analytics across India, beginning with West Bengal.

Founder Trustees: The first Board of Trustees of ASSOCADS has seven Founder Trustees, who serve without payment. The Board has elected its office bearers: Rahul Bhattacharya (President), Abhijit Pal (Vice-President), Prasun Nandy (Vice-President), Amit Kumar Das (General Secretary), Sandip Datta (Joint Secretary), Sayan Guha (Joint Secretary), Biswajeet Chaki (Treasurer). Five founder members serve on its sub-committees but are not on the Board. See the trustees

Membership: Eight individual and six organisational membership categories, approved by the Board in November 2026, from free Community membership upwards. Membership opens after registration. Honorary recognition, such as Fellow, is by invitation of the Board and is never bought. Categories and fees

Programme areas: Eight areas of work: training and certification, events and community, research and publications, industry and academia collaboration, responsible AI, startups and innovation, policy and advisory and recognition and AI for social good. All are planned; none has started yet.

Tax deductions: Not at present. ASSOCADS intends to apply for registration under sections 12AB and 80G of the Income Tax Act after the trust is registered. Until 80G approval is granted, donations do not qualify for a tax deduction.

Foreign contributions: No. ASSOCADS cannot accept foreign contributions until it holds registration or prior permission under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010.

Not affiliated with: No. ASSOCADS is an independent public charitable trust. It is not affiliated with, and does not speak for, the Association of Data Scientists (ADaSci), the Artificial Intelligence Association of India, the Analytics Society of India, NASSCOM, IAMAI or the Data Security Council of India (DSCI). It has no partners, members or supporters among these organisations, and their names appear here only to avoid confusion.

Our approach

# Building with AI, not just talking about it

ASSOCADS aims to help shape how AI and Data Science are learned, built, adopted and used to make a difference. This page sets out how its Founder Trustees want it to work, by building with AI rather than only talking about it, and the values they want it to stand for.

What sets us apart

## More than conferences and networking

Conferences, seminars, panels and networking events have their place, and ASSOCADS will hold them. But we do not want them to be what we are known for.

We want to create lasting, practical value that people associate with us. People should want to take part not only to attend events or join a network, but for what they can do here.

- Learnpractical skills from people who use them
- Buildworking solutions to real problems
- Experiencehow AI is used inside organisations
- Contributeknowledge, code and research to the field
- Achieverecognition that reflects what you can do

Proposals

## 12 ideas we plan to build on

Each belongs to one of our eight programmes. Partnerships with companies and colleges, and a growing membership, remain priorities alongside them.

These are proposals, not services

None of these has started. After registration, the Board will weigh them, choose the most practical ones to begin with, and build on them step by step. Not everything will start at once.

### Learn by doing

Learning that leaves you with skills and work you can show.

#### Hands-on masterclasses

Practical sessions led by experienced practitioners, where participants work on real business problems, build AI applications, try new tools and see how these technologies are used inside organisations.

You leave with working prototypes and skills you can show, not just slides.

Part of Training and certification

#### Practical certifications

Certifications that test what you can do as well as what you know: a proctored online theory examination, followed by a real-world problem or project assessed by experienced industry professionals against published criteria.

A certification that shows how well you apply your knowledge to real problems.

Part of Training and certification

#### Mentoring and career growth

Structured mentoring that pairs experienced architects, data scientists, researchers and leaders with students, young professionals and people moving into AI. Mentors help with practical projects, portfolios and what employers expect. Members also mentor each other across specialisations.

Real guidance and a portfolio of work, from people who do the job.

Part of Training and certification

### Build real solutions

Mixed teams from industry and academia, working on problems that matter to someone.

#### Collaborative use case development

Professionals from different companies work with students and researchers to build practical solutions to real business problems. Working prototypes are then shown to enterprises, mid-sized businesses and startups that might adopt or develop them further.

Cross-organisation teams that turn ideas into working prototypes.

Part of Industry and academia collaboration

#### Industry problem exchange

A structured way for companies to share specific business challenges that AI or Data Science might help solve. Members study them, suggest approaches, build prototypes and demonstrate possible solutions.

A steady link between what industry needs and what our community can do.

Part of Industry and academia collaboration

#### Innovation challenges and hackathons

Regular challenges built around real problems from companies, startups, government bodies and social organisations, for mixed teams of professionals, students, researchers and independent experts. The work does not end with the winners: we aim to help promising solutions find mentors, sponsors and first users.

Solutions that carry on after the event and get used.

Part of Events and community

#### Idea incubation and proofs of concept

Members submit AI ideas or early-stage solutions. A panel of experienced architects, data scientists, business leaders and technologists picks the most promising, and ASSOCADS helps with mentoring, technical guidance, industry connections and the chance to build a proof of concept.

A route from an individual idea to enterprises, customers and investors.

Part of Startups and innovation

#### Open-source contribution

Members contribute together to open-source projects, reusable frameworks, datasets, reference architectures, evaluation benchmarks and implementation templates, gathered in a shared repository for everyone to use.

Public work that builds your credibility and helps the wider community.

Part of Research and publications

### Share knowledge openly

Knowledge that stays available long after an event ends.

#### A knowledge and media platform

Podcasts, webinars, expert interviews, panel discussions and technology demonstrations, published on YouTube, LinkedIn and other channels as a permanent library anyone can use at any time.

Knowledge that reaches far beyond the people in the room.

Part of Events and community

#### An annual industry report

A yearly report on how AI and Data Science are being adopted, with emerging technologies, industry challenges, research and talent trends, drawing on members, industry, academic institutions and organisations in different sectors.

A dependable reference on the state of the field.

Part of Research and publications

### Serve industry and society

Help for organisations and communities that need it most.

#### A responsible AI working group

A dedicated group to research data privacy, security, ethics, bias, explainability and regulation, publish practical guidelines, and help businesses, especially small and medium ones, adopt AI responsibly, securely and within the law.

Practical help for organisations that want to use AI well.

Part of Responsible AI

#### AI for social good

Members volunteer their expertise to build affordable, practical solutions for NGOs, schools, local communities and public services, in areas such as education, healthcare, agriculture, sustainability and accessibility.

Advanced technology for people who could not otherwise reach it.

Part of Recognition and AI for social good

A closer look

## Certification that tests what you can do

Many certifications rely on theory, multiple-choice examinations and product-specific skills. We propose certifications in two parts, so that candidates show what they know and how well they apply it.

- PART 1

### Theory

An online, remotely proctored examination of the concepts, technologies and methods involved.

- PART 2

### Practical assessment

A real-world problem or project, evaluated by experienced industry professionals against clearly defined criteria.

- Our aim is rigorous standards, credible assessors and transparent criteria, so that over time employers can rely on these certifications when they hire for AI and Data Science roles.

Measuring success

## What we want to be judged by

Not only by how many conferences we hold, how many people attend or how many members we enrol, but by questions like these.

- 01How many practical AI and Data Science solutions have we helped create?
- 02How many businesses have we helped adopt AI?
- 03How many professionals and students have we helped develop?
- 04How much knowledge, research and intellectual contribution have we made to the field?
- 05How many meaningful collaborations have we made possible?
- 06How many ideas have we helped turn into working solutions?
- 07How much positive impact have we had on society?
- 08How many opportunities have we created for our members?

## One place to learn, experiment, collaborate and solve real problems

We want ASSOCADS to grow into a community where industry professionals, technologists, researchers, academics, students, startups and businesses come together, because they see something useful happening here. When people hear our name, we want them to think of practical knowledge, real contributions and real-world impact.

About

# Aims and objects

The trust deed sets out sixteen objects: the purposes ASSOCADS exists to pursue. Together they commit it to building a community for AI and Data Science in India that learns, researches, innovates and works for public good, always on a not-for-profit basis.

These objects are taken from the ASSOCADS trust deed and written here in plain English. The numbers match the deed, so each object can be cited. The deed itself remains the authoritative text.

## Community and learning

- 01

### An inclusive ecosystem

Bring together everyone working in AI, Data Science, Machine Learning and Analytics: students, professionals, academics, researchers, industry, entrepreneurs, investors, institutions and government.

Programme: Events and community

- 02

### Education and capacity building

Run conferences, seminars, workshops, bootcamps, hackathons, meetups and training. This includes certification, faculty development, mentoring, career guidance, internships and apprenticeships.

Programme: Training and certification, Events and community

- 14

### Training and advice by sector

Offer training and advisory services across industries, directly or through Special Interest Groups.

Programme: Training and certification

## Research and knowledge

- 05

### Research and publishing

Carry out research and publish it as journals, case studies, benchmark datasets, technical reports and white papers.

Programme: Research and publications

- 11

### Open and community-driven work

Encourage collaborative, open-source and community-led projects.

Programme: Research and publications

- 15

### Intellectual property

Create, protect and share intellectual property.

Programme: Research and publications

## Collaboration and policy

- 04

### Collaboration across sectors

Help academia, industry, government, civil society and international institutions work together.

Programme: Industry and academia collaboration

- 09

### National and international links

Work with organisations in India and abroad, and take part in global initiatives.

Programme: Industry and academia collaboration

- 10

### Policy and standards

Contribute to policies, standards, frameworks and good practice, and advise governments, institutions and industry.

Programme: Policy and advisory

## Innovation and recognition

- 07

### Innovation and entrepreneurship

Support innovation, incubation and new ventures, including mentoring, introductions to investors and access to markets.

Programme: Startups and innovation

- 08

### Recognising excellence

Recognise excellent work through awards, fellowships, certifications and accreditations.

Programme: Recognition and AI for social good

## Responsibility and public good

- 06

### Responsible AI

Promote AI and Data Science that is responsible, ethical, transparent and trustworthy.

Programme: Responsible AI

- 12

### AI for social good

Design and support projects that use AI for public benefit: in healthcare, agriculture, education, governance, sustainability, climate resilience, public welfare, accessibility, rural development and social inclusion.

Programme: Recognition and AI for social good

## Institutions and support

- 03

### Centres, labs and hubs

Set up or support centres, labs, academies, libraries and knowledge repositories, along with innovation hubs, incubation centres and Centres of Excellence.

Programme: Research and publications

- 13

### Institutions and infrastructure

Set up or support the institutions, facilities and infrastructure that these objects need.

- 16

### Other lawful activities

Do anything else that is lawful and supports these objects, always on a not-for-profit basis.

Questions

## Questions

All questions

**What does ASSOCADS plan to do?**

The trust deed sets out sixteen objects, which ASSOCADS groups into eight programme areas: training and certification; events and community; research and publications; industry and academia collaboration; responsible AI; startups and innovation; policy and advisory; and recognition and AI for social good. All eight are planned, and the site states clearly when any activity starts.

About

# Governance

ASSOCADS is governed by its Board of Trustees under a trust deed, and is run on a not-for-profit basis. This page explains who is responsible, the principles that bind the trust, how its money is to be accounted for, and which documents it will publish as they are adopted.

Last updated 24 November 2026

Registration in progress

## Legal status

Status: ASSOCADS is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026. Its registration is in progress.

Tax deductions: Not at present. ASSOCADS intends to apply for registration under sections 12AB and 80G of the Income Tax Act after the trust is registered. Until 80G approval is granted, donations do not qualify for a tax deduction.

Foreign contributions: No. ASSOCADS cannot accept foreign contributions until it holds registration or prior permission under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010.

How it works

## How the trust is run

These rules come from the trust deed. Because the trust is new, they describe what the deed requires rather than a record of past practice.

### A public charitable trust

ASSOCADS is a public charitable trust. It is non-political, non-religious, not-for-profit and irrevocable: once made, the trust cannot be taken back by the people who set it up.

### The Board of Trustees

The trust is managed by a Board of between seven and fifteen trustees. The first Board has seven Founder Trustees.

Meet the trustees

### Office bearers

The Board elects its office bearers for terms of two years:

- One President
- Up to two Vice-Presidents
- One General Secretary
- Up to two Joint Secretaries
- One Treasurer

The Board has elected:

President:: Rahul Bhattacharya

Vice-Presidents:: Abhijit Pal and Prasun Nandy

General Secretary:: Amit Kumar Das

Joint Secretaries:: Sandip Datta and Sayan Guha

Treasurer:: Biswajeet Chaki

### Honorary trustees

Trustees are honorary. They receive no payment for acting as trustees.

### Meetings

The Board meets at least once every quarter.

### Audit and annual report

The accounts must be audited every year by a Chartered Accountant, and the Board adopts an annual report. The financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.

### Members and the Board

Membership gives no share in the trust's funds and no right to manage the trust or to vote, unless bye-laws later provide otherwise. The Board may set up chapters in other states and cities, Special Interest Groups and advisory councils.

### If the trust is dissolved

Its assets pass to a similar charitable institution. They can never go to the trustees or the members.

Principles

## Ten principles that bind the trust

The trust deed commits ASSOCADS to these principles in everything it does.

- 01

### Compliance with the law

The trust acts within the law at all times.

- 02

### Open to all

Its programmes and membership are open to everyone, without discrimination.

- 03

### Not for profit

It works on a not-for-profit basis. Its assets can never be shared among trustees or members.

- 04

### Responsible AI

It promotes AI that is responsible, ethical, transparent and trustworthy.

- 05

### Data protection

It protects the personal data it holds.

- 06

### Conflicts of interest

Trustees follow the conflict-of-interest rules set in the trust deed.

- 07

### Academic integrity

Its research, training and publications uphold academic integrity.

- 08

### Proper approvals

It obtains the approvals and permissions its activities need.

- 09

### A focus on society

Its work is aimed at public benefit.

- 10

### Tax registration

It intends to apply for registration under sections 12AB and 80G of the Income Tax Act.

Documents

## Documents

We will publish these documents here as they become available.

### Certificate of registration

Proof that the trust is registered. Published once registration is complete.

To be published

### Bye-laws

The trust's rules, including membership and committees, adopted by the Board after registration.

To be published

### Annual report 2026–27

What the trust did in its first financial year, adopted by the Board.

To be published

### Audited accounts 2026–27

The first year's accounts, audited by a Chartered Accountant.

To be published

Questions

## Questions

All questions

**Who runs ASSOCADS?**

ASSOCADS is run by a Board of Trustees. The first Board has seven Founder Trustees, named on the Founder Trustees page. The Board has elected its office bearers: Rahul Bhattacharya is President, Abhijit Pal and Prasun Nandy are Vice-Presidents, Amit Kumar Das is General Secretary, Sandip Datta and Sayan Guha are Joint Secretaries, and Biswajeet Chaki is Treasurer. Five founder members work with the trustees on its sub-committees but are not on the Board.

**Are the trustees paid?**

No. Trustees are honorary and receive no payment for acting as trustees.

**Is ASSOCADS political or religious?**

No. ASSOCADS is non-political, non-religious and not-for-profit. It is open to everyone, without discrimination.

**Can members vote or help manage ASSOCADS?**

No. ASSOCADS is a trust, not a society, so it is managed by its Board of Trustees. Membership gives access to programmes and benefits, but no ownership, no share of any surplus and no seat on the Board. Some members may be invited to advisory councils, which advise the Board.

# Founder Trustees and founder members

The first Board of Trustees of ASSOCADS has seven Founder Trustees. Three of them are also Settlors, the people who created the trust. They serve in an honorary capacity, without payment. The Board has elected its office bearers, shown on each card with the sub-committees each person serves on.

## Amit Kumar Das

Settlor and Founder Trustee

General Secretary

Co-founder and Director, Quantyra Analytics

Dr Amit Kumar Das has worked in data science in industry and in academic research and teaching for more than 28 years. He is also Professor and Dean, Industry Consultancy, at the Institute of Engineering & Management, and was previously a Principal Director at LTIMindtree. He holds a PhD in machine learning from the University of Calcutta, has written data science and AI textbooks published by Pearson, and is a Senior Member of IEEE.

- Data science
- Machine learning
- Deep learning
- Big data

## Abhijit Pal

Settlor and Founder Trustee

Vice-President

Director and Chief of Strategy, Growth and Innovation, XEqualTo Analytics

Abhijit Pal has about 27 years of experience in technology consulting, covering IT and digital strategy, implementation and value realisation for clients in India and abroad, across government, retail, healthcare, education, telecommunications and manufacturing. He now leads strategy at an Indian data, analytics and AI company, mentors startups and students, and is an honorary adviser to the IT Committee of the Bengal Chamber of Commerce and Industry. He graduated in Electronics and Instrumentation Engineering from Jadavpur University.

- Technology and digital strategy
- Enterprise architecture
- Analytics and AI
- AI in healthcare

**Who runs ASSOCADS?**

ASSOCADS is run by a Board of Trustees. The first Board has seven Founder Trustees, named on the Founder Trustees page. The Board has elected its office bearers: Rahul Bhattacharya is President, Abhijit Pal and Prasun Nandy are Vice-Presidents, Amit Kumar Das is General Secretary, Sandip Datta and Sayan Guha are Joint Secretaries, and Biswajeet Chaki is Treasurer. Five founder members work with the trustees on its sub-committees but are not on the Board.

About

# Roadmap

The ASSOCADS roadmap sets out what the trust plans to do in three stages: getting established in the first twelve months, running its first programmes in the second year, and widening its reach after that. Every item on it is a plan, not something that has already happened.

This roadmap sets out intentions. Dates and details will be confirmed by the Board.

- 01 · Near term · First 12 months

## Getting established

- Complete the registration of the trust.
- Open membership in the categories, at the fees, that the Board approved in November 2026.
- Apply for registration under sections 12AB and 80G of the Income Tax Act.
- Have our first year's accounts audited and adopt our first annual report after the financial year ends on 31 March.

- 02 · Mid term · 12 to 24 months

## First programmes

- Run our first workshops, meetups and hackathons, beginning in West Bengal.
- Form Special Interest Groups by industry or domain.
- Publish our first research reports, each reviewed by a trustee.
- Start training, mentoring and faculty development programmes with colleges and universities.
- Build working links between academia, industry, startups and government.
- Share plain-English guidance on responsible AI.

- 03 · Long term · Beyond 24 months

## Wider reach

- Set up chapters in other states and cities.
- Establish or support Centres of Excellence, labs and incubation hubs.
- Grow into an apex professional body for AI and Data Science in India.
- Support startups through mentoring, investor engagement and market access.
- Contribute to policies, standards and frameworks, and advise governments and institutions.
- Introduce awards and fellowships, and support AI-for-social-good projects.

Questions

## Questions

All questions

**What does ASSOCADS plan to do?**

The trust deed sets out sixteen objects, which ASSOCADS groups into eight programme areas: training and certification; events and community; research and publications; industry and academia collaboration; responsible AI; startups and innovation; policy and advisory; and recognition and AI for social good. All eight are planned, and the site states clearly when any activity starts.

# Programmes

ASSOCADS groups the sixteen objects of its trust deed into eight programme areas, from training and research to responsible AI and policy. All of them are planned: each will begin after the trust is registered, and its page will say when. Each page sets out what the programme aims to do and how it plans to work.

## All programmes

Planned

### Training and certification

Workshops, bootcamps, mentoring and certification

- Planned

### Events and community

- Planned

### Industry and academia collaboration

Knowledge exchange and workforce readiness

- Planned

### Responsible AI

Fairness, accountability, privacy and governance

- Planned

### Startups and innovation

Mentoring, incubation and investor engagement

- Planned

### Policy and advisory

Standards, frameworks and guidance for institutions

Awards, fellowships and projects for public benefit

## How the programmes map to the trust's objects

Every programme carries out one or more objects of the trust deed. The numbers match the deed.

### Training and certification

- 02Education and capacity building
- 14Training and advice by sector

- 02Education and capacity building

**What does ASSOCADS plan to do?**

The trust deed sets out sixteen objects, which ASSOCADS groups into eight programme areas: training and certification; events and community; research and publications; industry and academia collaboration; responsible AI; startups and innovation; policy and advisory; and recognition and AI for social good. All eight are planned, and the site states clearly when any activity starts.

**What programmes does ASSOCADS plan to run?**

ASSOCADS plans to work in eight areas: events and community; training and certification; research and publications; responsible AI; industry and academia collaboration; startups and innovation; policy and advisory; and recognition and AI for social good. The programmes page describes each area and says whether work has started.

**Does ASSOCADS award certificates?**

The trust deed allows ASSOCADS to offer training and certification, and the trust plans to do so. Any certificate will be announced on this website, with what it covers and who awards it. ASSOCADS does not issue certificates at present.

Programme

# Training and certification

Training and certification is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to help students, professionals and teachers build practical skills in AI, Data Science and Analytics. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Planned

Plans

## What this will include

We plan to help students and working professionals build practical skills in AI, data science and analytics. The trust deed provides for workshops, bootcamps, training courses and certification, along with faculty development for teachers, mentoring, career guidance, internships and apprenticeships. It also allows training and advisory services for specific industries, offered directly or through Special Interest Groups. Courses, formats and any fees will be decided by the Board and announced on this site before they open.

- Workshops, bootcamps and training courses in AI, Data Science and Analytics.
- Hands-on masterclasses led by industry practitioners, built around real business problems.
- Practical certifications in two parts, a proctored theory examination and a real-world project assessed by industry professionals.
- Faculty development for teachers in colleges and universities.
- Structured mentoring and career guidance, including help with practical projects and portfolios, and peer mentoring between members.
- Internships and apprenticeships.
- Training and advisory services for specific industries, directly or through Special Interest Groups.

Based on the trust deed: object 2, education and capacity building, object 14, training and advice by sector.

## Who it is for

- For studentsLearn practical AI and data science skills, find mentors, and meet the people already working in the field.
- For professionalsFor practitioners, faculty and researchers who want to keep learning, share what they know and help shape the field.
- For industryFor companies and startups looking to hire, train their teams, work with researchers or support the community.

Status

## Planned

This programme is planned and has not started yet. It will begin after ASSOCADS is registered, and details will be published on this page.

Get involved

## How to get involved

Training begins after the trust is registered. Register your interest and we will tell you when the first courses open. Colleges and companies that would like to host or shape a course can talk to us about a partnership.

Register your interestPartner with us

Questions

## Questions about this programme

**Are ASSOCADS courses open yet?**

Not yet. Training will begin after the trust is registered. Courses, formats and dates will be announced on this page before they open.

**Will ASSOCADS certificates be recognised?**

ASSOCADS has not issued any certificates yet. How certification will work, and what it will cover, will be decided by the Board and explained here before any course opens.

**How much will training cost?**

No fees have been set. The Board will decide any fees after registration and publish them here before a course opens.

**Is there anything for teachers?**

Yes. The trust deed provides for faculty development, so that teachers in colleges and universities can build their own skills in AI and data science.

## Related programmes

- Events and communityConferences, seminars, meetups and hackathons
- Industry and academia collaborationKnowledge exchange and workforce readiness
- Research and publicationsReports, white papers, datasets and open-source work

# Events and community

Events and community is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to bring together everyone working in AI and Data Science in India, beginning in West Bengal, so they can meet, learn and build together. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Planned

Plans

## What this will include

We aim to bring together the people who work with AI and data in India, starting in West Bengal: students, professionals, academics, researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, institutions and government. The trust deed provides for conferences, seminars, meetups and hackathons as the main ways to do this. No events have been held yet. Each event will be listed on this site, with its date, venue and how to register, once it has been confirmed.

- Conferences and seminars.
- Meetups for people working in AI, Data Science and Analytics.
- Innovation challenges and hackathons on real problems, with help afterwards for promising solutions to find mentors, sponsors and first users.
- Workshops that bring students, professionals and researchers together.
- Podcasts, webinars, expert interviews and technology demonstrations, published online as a permanent library.
- A community that connects academia, industry, entrepreneurs, investors, institutions and government.

Based on the trust deed: object 1, an inclusive ecosystem, object 2, education and capacity building.

## Who it is for

- For studentsLearn practical AI and data science skills, find mentors, and meet the people already working in the field.
- For professionalsFor practitioners, faculty and researchers who want to keep learning, share what they know and help shape the field.
- For industryFor companies and startups looking to hire, train their teams, work with researchers or support the community.
- For government bodiesFor departments and public institutions interested in policy support, capacity building and AI for the public good.

Status

## Planned

This programme is planned and has not started yet. It will begin after ASSOCADS is registered, and details will be published on this page.

Get involved

## How to get involved

No events have been announced yet. Register your interest to hear about the first ones. Organisations that would like to host or support an event can talk to us about a partnership.

Register your interestPartner with us

No event has been announced yet. We plan to announce our first events after the trust is registered. Each one will be listed on the events page with its date, venue and how to register.

**Do I need to be a member to attend?**

That has not been decided yet. Each event page will say who can attend and how to register.

**Where will events take place?**

We plan to begin in West Bengal. Each event page will give its venue, or say if it is held online.

# Research and publications

Research and publications is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to produce and share research on AI and Data Science that others can use. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Planned

Plans

## What this will include

We plan to carry out and publish useful research on AI and data science. The trust deed provides for journals, case studies, benchmark datasets, technical reports and white papers, and for collaborative, open-source and community-driven work. It also allows the trust to set up or support labs, libraries, knowledge repositories and Centres of Excellence, and to create, protect and share intellectual property. No research reports have been published yet; each will appear here when it is ready. Our practical guides are on the guides page.

- Research published as journals, case studies, technical reports and white papers.
- Benchmark datasets.
- An open-source contribution programme for frameworks, datasets, reference architectures, evaluation benchmarks and templates in a shared repository.
- An annual report on AI and Data Science adoption, technologies, talent and research.
- Labs, libraries, knowledge repositories and Centres of Excellence, set up or supported by the trust.
- Creating, protecting and sharing intellectual property.

Based on the trust deed: object 3, centres, labs and hubs, object 5, research and publishing, object 11, open and community-driven work, object 15, intellectual property.

## Who it is for

- For studentsLearn practical AI and data science skills, find mentors, and meet the people already working in the field.
- For professionalsFor practitioners, faculty and researchers who want to keep learning, share what they know and help shape the field.
- For industryFor companies and startups looking to hire, train their teams, work with researchers or support the community.

Status

## Planned

This programme is planned and has not started yet. It will begin after ASSOCADS is registered, and details will be published on this page.

Not yet. Each publication will appear on this site when it is ready, and every guide or article will be reviewed by a named trustee before it is published.

**Will ASSOCADS research be free to read?**

We aim to share research openly where we can. The terms for each publication will be stated when it is released.

**Can I contribute to an ASSOCADS project?**

The trust deed encourages collaborative, open-source and community-driven work. How people can contribute will be explained here when the first projects start.

Industry and academia collaboration is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to help academia, industry, government and civil society work together, so that knowledge flows both ways. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Plans

The trust deed also provides for collaboration with national and international organisations and for taking part in global initiatives. Any partner will be named on this site only after a formal agreement and written permission are in place. No partnerships have been announced so far.

- Collaboration between academia, industry, government and civil society.
- Knowledge exchange between universities, colleges and companies.
- Joint use case development, where professionals from different companies work with students and researchers on real business problems.
- An exchange where companies share problem statements, and members propose approaches and build prototypes.
- Work with international institutions.
- Collaboration with national and international organisations.
- Taking part in global initiatives in AI and Data Science.

Programme

# Responsible AI

Responsible AI is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to promote AI and Data Science that is responsible, ethical, transparent and trustworthy. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Planned

Plans

## What this will include

We plan to promote AI and data science that is responsible, ethical, transparent and trustworthy. This covers questions of fairness, accountability, privacy, security and governance, and helping the public understand what these systems can and cannot do. Responsible AI is also one of the principles that bind the trust itself, under its deed. We intend to publish plain-English explainers and practical guidance, each reviewed by a named trustee before it appears on this site, for readers in industry and government.

- Plain-English guidance on fairness and accountability in AI systems.
- Material on privacy and security in AI and data work.
- Guidance on the governance of AI in organisations.
- A working group on privacy, security, bias, explainability and regulation, publishing practical guidelines.
- Help for small and medium businesses to adopt AI responsibly, securely and within the law.
- Public awareness of what AI systems can and cannot do.

Based on the trust deed: object 6, responsible ai.

## Our own commitment

Responsible AI is not only something ASSOCADS promotes. It is one of the principles that bind the trust itself under its deed.

We intend to hold our own work to the same standard we promote. The guides we publish, the events we run and any AI tools we use or build should be responsible, ethical, transparent and trustworthy. The deed also binds the trust to data protection, academic integrity and conflict-of-interest rules. Read more about how the trust is run.

## Who it is for

- For studentsLearn practical AI and data science skills, find mentors, and meet the people already working in the field.
- For professionalsFor practitioners, faculty and researchers who want to keep learning, share what they know and help shape the field.
- For industryFor companies and startups looking to hire, train their teams, work with researchers or support the community.
- For government bodiesFor departments and public institutions interested in policy support, capacity building and AI for the public good.

Status

## Planned

This programme is planned and has not started yet. It will begin after ASSOCADS is registered, and details will be published on this page.

Get involved

## How to get involved

Our practical guides are published on the guides page, each reviewed by a named trustee. Organisations that would like to discuss responsible AI with us can get in touch.

Read the guidesContact us

Questions

## Questions about this programme

**What does ASSOCADS mean by responsible AI?**

AI and data science that is responsible, ethical, transparent and trustworthy. In practice this covers fairness, accountability, privacy, security and governance.

**Does ASSOCADS follow these principles itself?**

Yes. Responsible AI is one of the principles that bind the trust under its deed, alongside data protection, academic integrity and conflict-of-interest rules.

**Has ASSOCADS published guidance yet?**

Yes. Practical guides, including ones on India's data protection law and on the regulation of AI, are on the guides page. Each was reviewed by a named trustee before it appeared on this site. Guidance written for organisations by the proposed working group is still a plan.

## Related programmes

- Policy and advisoryStandards, frameworks and guidance for institutions
- Research and publicationsReports, white papers, datasets and open-source work
- Recognition and AI for social goodAwards, fellowships and projects for public benefit

# Startups and innovation

Startups and innovation is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to support innovation, incubation and new ventures in AI and Data Science. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Planned

Plans

## What this will include

We aim to support innovation and entrepreneurship in AI and data science, with an initial focus on founders in West Bengal. The trust deed provides for mentoring, incubation, engagement with investors and help with market access. The form this support takes, and who can apply for it, will be decided by the Board after the trust is registered. Until then this programme is planned, and no incubation places, funding or investor introductions are being offered.

- Mentoring for founders.
- Incubation support.
- Engagement with investors.
- Help with access to markets.
- Support for innovation in AI and Data Science.
- A proof-of-concept programme, in which members submit ideas, an expert panel picks promising ones, and the trust helps them become working prototypes.

Based on the trust deed: object 7, innovation and entrepreneurship.

## Who it is for

- For studentsLearn practical AI and data science skills, find mentors, and meet the people already working in the field.
- For professionalsFor practitioners, faculty and researchers who want to keep learning, share what they know and help shape the field.

Not yet. Who can apply, and how, will be decided by the Board after the trust is registered and published on this page.

**Does ASSOCADS invest in startups?**

No. ASSOCADS is a not-for-profit trust. The trust deed provides for engagement with investors, not for the trust to invest itself.

**Does ASSOCADS run an incubator?**

Not at present. The trust deed allows it to set up or support incubation centres, and any plans will be announced here.

# Policy and advisory

Policy and advisory is one of the eight planned programme areas of ASSOCADS. It aims to help shape the policies, standards and practices that govern how AI and Data Science are used in India. It has not started yet, and will begin after the trust is registered.

Planned

Plans

## What this will include

We plan to contribute to the policies, standards, frameworks and good practices that shape how AI and data science are used in India. The trust deed provides for advising governments, public institutions and industry on these questions. We expect this work to draw on the experience of our trustees and members, and to be published openly where it can be. No advisory engagements have been undertaken yet. Any that are agreed will be described here.

- Contributions to policies on AI and Data Science.
- Work on standards and frameworks.
- Sharing good practice.
- Advice to governments and public institutions.
- Advice to industry.

Based on the trust deed: object 10, policy and standards.

## Who it is for

- For professionalsFor practitioners, faculty and researchers who want to keep learning, share what they know and help shape the field.
- For industryFor companies and startups looking to hire, train their teams, work with researchers or support the community.
- For government bodiesFor departments and public institutions interested in policy support, capacity building and AI for the public good.

## Questions about this programme

Not yet. Advising governments and public institutions is one of the trust's objects. Any advisory work that is agreed will be described on this page.

**Is ASSOCADS political?**

No. ASSOCADS is non-political, non-religious and not-for-profit. Its policy work will focus on the use of AI and data science.

**Will ASSOCADS publish its policy work?**

We aim to publish it openly where we can. Each publication will be reviewed by a named trustee before it appears here.

Source: {{SITE_URL}}/membership

Membership

# Membership

Membership of ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science, is for individuals and organisations: students, academics, professionals, independents, institutions, startups, companies and public bodies. The Board approved these categories and fees in November 2026. Membership opens after the trust is registered.

Last updated 26 November 2026

Register your interest

Membership opens after registration

The categories and fees on this page are approved, but no fee is collected yet. Register your interest and we will write to you when applications open. Benefits begin as each programme starts.

## How membership is organised

Each member is either an individual or an organisation, and belongs to one of six verticals.

The six verticals, with the individual and organisational category in each
| Vertical | Individual | Organisation |

| Education | Student (undergraduate, postgraduate, PhD or diploma) | Academic Institution (school, college or university) |

| Academia and research | Academic (faculty, researchers and post-doctoral fellows) | Research Lab or Institute |

| Industry | Professional (Early-career, Mid-career, or Senior or Leader) | Corporate (MSME, Mid-size or Enterprise) |

| Entrepreneurship | Independent (freelancers, consultants and founders) | Startup (DPIIT-recognised, or under five years old) |

| Public and social | Public-interest (NGO staff, journalists, public servants and retired professionals) | Non-profit, Government or PSU body |

| Ecosystem | Not applicable | Community, Event or Media Partner |

- Education

Individual: Student (undergraduate, postgraduate, PhD or diploma)

Organisation: Academic Institution (school, college or university)

- Academia and research

Individual: Academic (faculty, researchers and post-doctoral fellows)

Organisation: Research Lab or Institute

- Industry

Individual: Professional (Early-career, Mid-career, or Senior or Leader)

Organisation: Corporate (MSME, Mid-size or Enterprise)

For individuals

## Individual membership

All fees are in Indian rupees, for one year and before any applicable taxes, unless stated otherwise.

### Community

Anyone who registers.

Free

Includes: Newsletter, public events, viewing the job board, and the forum.

### Student

Enrolled in an undergraduate, postgraduate, PhD or diploma course, with a valid ID.

₹600 a year₹300 through a member institution

Includes: Competitions, hackathons, mentorship, the learning library and the internship board.

### Academic

Faculty, researchers and post-doctoral fellows.

₹2,000 a year

Includes: Faculty development programmes at the member price, research collaboration, the publication and reviewer pool, and academic forums.

### Professional: Early-career

Under five years of experience.

₹1,500 a year

Includes: Networking, discounted events and training, posting on the job board, and the mentee track.

### Professional: Mid-career

Five to twelve years of experience.

₹3,000 a year

Includes: Early-career benefits, plus the speaker pool, the mentor track and certification discounts.

### Professional: Senior or Leader

Over twelve years of experience, or a CXO, Director or Principal.

₹6,000 a year

Includes: Mid-career benefits, plus leadership roundtables and advisory panels.

### Independent

Freelancers, consultants, solo founders and people changing careers.

₹2,000 a year

Includes: Professional benefits, plus the consultant directory and the referral board.

### Public-interest

NGO staff, journalists, public servants and retired professionals.

₹1,000 a year

Includes: Professional benefits, plus the AI-for-good and policy working groups.

Every paid individual member receives a digital membership certificate and a member ID that can be verified.

## How long you can join for

Join for one year, or for longer at a lower price.

Membership tenure: duration, price and extras
| Tenure | Duration | Price | Extras |

| Annual | 12 months | The annual fee | None |

| Multi-year | 3 years | 2.7 times the annual fee (a 10% saving) | The fee is locked for the term. |

| Long-term | 5 years, the longest available | 4 times the annual fee (a 20% saving) | The fee is locked, plus a Long-Term Member badge, priority seats at events and one free upgrade of category. |

| Course-duration (students only) | Until the course ends, up to 4 years | The annual fee for each year, less 15% | Converts to Early-career Professional at half price for the first year after graduation. |

- Annual

Duration: 12 months

Price: The annual fee

Extras: None

- Multi-year

Duration: 3 years

Price: 2.7 times the annual fee (a 10% saving)

Extras: The fee is locked for the term.

- Long-term

Duration: 5 years, the longest available

Price: 4 times the annual fee (a 20% saving)

Extras: The fee is locked, plus a Long-Term Member badge, priority seats at events and one free upgrade of category.

- Course-duration (students only)

Duration: Until the course ends, up to 4 years

Price: The annual fee for each year, less 15%

Extras: Converts to Early-career Professional at half price for the first year after graduation.

For example, a Mid-career Professional pays ₹3,000 for one year, ₹8,100 for three years or ₹12,000 for five years. There is no lifetime membership.

## Concessions

Ways to pay less, so that cost does not keep anyone out.

### Access seats

Each year, 10% of paid seats are free or half price for students from economically weaker backgrounds, students at rural and Tier-3 institutions, women returning to work, persons with disabilities and first-generation graduates.

### Founding cohort

The first 500 individuals and the first 25 organisations in the first year get 30% off any tenure, and a Founding Cohort badge.

### Referral

Bring in three paid members and your next year is free.

### Group

Ten or more individuals from one employer get 15% off.

### International

Individuals outside India pay USD 50 a year as a Professional or USD 20 as a Student. Organisations outside India pay by quotation.

### Upgrade credit

When you move to a higher category during your term, the unused value of your membership is credited.

To be clear

## What membership is not

ASSOCADS is a charitable trust. Membership gives access to programmes and benefits. It gives no ownership, no share of any surplus and no seat on the Board of Trustees.

This is normal for a public charitable trust. Unlike a society or a company, a trust has no shareholders or voting members. It is run by its Board of Trustees, who must use its money only for its charitable objects.

Membership is a way to take part in what ASSOCADS does, not to own or control it. How the trust is run

## Honorary recognition

Honorary recognition is separate from paid membership and is never bought.

| Volunteer Leader | Volunteers who have served a chapter, Special Interest Group or committee for over 12 months. | Fee waived while serving | A leadership certificate and recognition. |

## Joining and membership rules

- 01

### Apply

Fill in the online form with your category, proof of eligibility and acceptance of the Code of Conduct.

- 02

### Approval

The Membership sub-committee decides on individual applications within 7 days. Organisations hear within 21 days, with the sign-off of one Board member.

- 03

### Onboarding

You receive a receipt, a digital certificate and a member ID, and are invited to a welcome session within 30 days.

- 04

### Renewal

We remind you 60, 30 and 7 days before your membership ends. A 30-day grace period follows, with your benefits intact.

- 05

### Lapse

After the grace period you return to free Community membership. If you rejoin within 12 months, you keep your seniority.

- 06

### Upgrade

You can move to a higher category at any time, and the unused value is credited.

- 07

### Termination

For a breach of the Code of Conduct or acting against the trust's objects, by resolution of the Board, after written notice and a chance to respond. There is no refund.

- 08

### Refunds

A pro-rata refund within 30 days of joining. After that, fees are not refundable, but an organisation's membership can be transferred within the same organisation.

Questions

## Questions about membership

All questions

**Who can join ASSOCADS?**

Individuals and organisations. Individuals can join as Community (free), Student, Academic, Professional (Early-career, Mid-career, or Senior or Leader), Independent or Public-interest members. Organisations can join as an Academic Institution, Research Lab or Institute, Startup, Corporate, Non-profit, Government or PSU body, or Community, Event or Media Partner. Honorary recognition, such as Fellow, is by invitation of the Board. Membership opens after the trust is registered.

**How much does membership cost?**

The Board approved the fees in November 2026. For individuals, Community membership is free, Student membership is ₹600 a year and Professional membership is ₹1,500 to ₹6,000 a year, depending on experience. Organisations pay from ₹5,000 a year for a startup to ₹4,00,000 a year for a large company. Fees are before any applicable taxes, and longer terms and concessions cost less. The membership page lists every category. No fee is collected until membership opens after registration.

**Is there a student membership?**

Yes. Student membership is for anyone enrolled in an undergraduate, postgraduate, PhD or diploma course, with a valid ID. It costs ₹600 a year, or ₹300 through a member institution, and students can join for the length of their course at 15% off. Membership opens after the trust is registered, and you can register your interest now.

**How do I become a member?**

Membership opens after the trust is registered. You will then apply online with your category, proof of eligibility and acceptance of the Code of Conduct. The Membership sub-committee decides on individual applications within 7 days, and organisations hear within 21 days. Until then, you can register your interest on the membership page, and we will write to you when applications open.

**Can members vote or help manage ASSOCADS?**

No. ASSOCADS is a trust, not a society, so it is managed by its Board of Trustees. Membership gives access to programmes and benefits, but no ownership, no share of any surplus and no seat on the Board. Some members may be invited to advisory councils, which advise the Board.

**Can a company or institution join?**

Yes. Organisations can join as an Academic Institution, Research Lab or Institute, Startup, Corporate, Non-profit, Government or PSU body, or Community, Event or Media Partner. Each membership includes seats for people the organisation names. The membership page lists the bands and fees. Applications open after the trust is registered.

**How does a membership end?**

A membership ends if it is not renewed: after a 30-day grace period, the member returns to free Community membership, and rejoining within 12 months keeps their seniority. The Board can also end a membership for a breach of the Code of Conduct or for acting against the trust's objects, after written notice and a chance to respond. In that case there is no refund.

**Are membership fees refundable?**

A pro-rata refund is available within 30 days of joining. After that, fees are not refundable, but an organisation's membership can be transferred within the same organisation. No fee is collected until membership opens after registration.

**Is a partnership the same as organisational membership?**

No. Organisational membership is a category of membership, with an annual fee, that gives an organisation's people access to programmes and benefits. A partnership is a written agreement to work together on something specific, such as a series of workshops or a research project.

## Be among the first members

Membership opens after registration. Register your interest now and we will write to you when applications open. The first 500 individuals and 25 organisations get 30% off.

Questions

# Frequently asked questions

This page answers the questions people ask most often about ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science: what it is, its legal status, who can join, what it plans to do, how to partner with or support it, and how this website treats your data. Each answer is short and stands on its own.

Find a question

42 questions in 6 groups.

## About ASSOCADS

**What is ASSOCADS?**

ASSOCADS, the Association for AI and Data Science, is a not-for-profit public charitable trust set up in Kolkata in 2026. It aims to build a collaborative ecosystem for AI, Data Science and Analytics across India, beginning with West Bengal, that connects students, professionals, academia, industry, startups, government and society.

Link to this question

**Is ASSOCADS registered?**

ASSOCADS is a not-for-profit public charitable trust established in Kolkata, West Bengal, India, in 2026. Its registration is in progress.

Link to this question

**Where is ASSOCADS based?**

ASSOCADS was set up in Kolkata, and its registered office is in West Bengal. Its work is meant to serve people across India, beginning with West Bengal.

Link to this question

**What does ASSOCADS plan to do?**

The trust deed sets out sixteen objects, which ASSOCADS groups into eight programme areas: training and certification; events and community; research and publications; industry and academia collaboration; responsible AI; startups and innovation; policy and advisory; and recognition and AI for social good. All eight are planned, and the site states clearly when any activity starts.

Link to this question

**Who runs ASSOCADS?**

ASSOCADS is run by a Board of Trustees. The first Board has seven Founder Trustees, named on the Founder Trustees page. The Board has elected its office bearers: Rahul Bhattacharya is President, Abhijit Pal and Prasun Nandy are Vice-Presidents, Amit Kumar Das is General Secretary, Sandip Datta and Sayan Guha are Joint Secretaries, and Biswajeet Chaki is Treasurer. Five founder members work with the trustees on its sub-committees but are not on the Board.

Link to this question

**Are the trustees paid?**

No. Trustees are honorary and receive no payment for acting as trustees.

Link to this question

**Is ASSOCADS political or religious?**

No. ASSOCADS is non-political, non-religious and not-for-profit. It is open to everyone, without discrimination.

Link to this question

**Is ASSOCADS affiliated with ADaSci, the Artificial Intelligence Association of India, the Analytics Society of India, NASSCOM, IAMAI or DSCI?**

No. ASSOCADS is an independent public charitable trust. It is not affiliated with, and does not speak for, the Association of Data Scientists (ADaSci), the Artificial Intelligence Association of India, the Analytics Society of India, NASSCOM, IAMAI or the Data Security Council of India (DSCI). It has no partners, members or supporters among these organisations, and their names appear here only to avoid confusion.

Link to this question

**How is ASSOCADS different from industry bodies such as NASSCOM and IAMAI?**

NASSCOM and IAMAI are industry bodies whose members are companies. ASSOCADS is a public charitable trust governed by a trust deed, and its membership, which opens after registration, is for individuals, including students, as well as institutions and companies. Its work covers training, research, responsible AI, startups, policy and social good across academia, industry and government.

Link to this question

**How do I contact ASSOCADS?**

Use the form on the Contact page and choose what your message is about, so that it reaches the people who can answer it.

Link to this question

**What is the address of ASSOCADS?**

ASSOCADS has its registered office in West Bengal. The full address will be published on the Contact page once it is confirmed.

Link to this question

**I am a journalist. How do I reach ASSOCADS?**

Use the form on the Contact page and choose Media as the topic, so that your message is handled as a media enquiry.

Link to this question

**What is a Special Interest Group?**

A group for people who work in, or care about, one industry or domain, such as healthcare or financial services. The trust deed allows the Board to set them up and to offer training and advice through them. None has been formed yet.

Link to this question

**Can I start a Special Interest Group or a chapter?**

## Programmes and events

**What programmes does ASSOCADS plan to run?**

ASSOCADS plans to work in eight areas: events and community; training and certification; research and publications; responsible AI; industry and academia collaboration; startups and innovation; policy and advisory; and recognition and AI for social good. The programmes page describes each area and says whether work has started.

Link to this question

**Where can I find ASSOCADS events?**

Every announced event is listed on the events page, with its date, place and how to register. An event appears there only once its details are confirmed.

Link to this question

**Does ASSOCADS award certificates?**

The trust deed allows ASSOCADS to offer training and certification, and the trust plans to do so. Any certificate will be announced on this website, with what it covers and who awards it. ASSOCADS does not issue certificates at present.

Link to this question

**Who checks the guides on this website?**

Every guide is reviewed by a named trustee before it is published, and the reviewer's name is shown on the guide. Guides are general information, not legal, financial or career advice.

Link to this question

## Partnerships

**How do I propose a partnership with ASSOCADS?**

Fill in the partnership enquiry on the Partner with us page. We start with a conversation, then put a proposal in writing. A partnership begins only when a written agreement has been approved by the Board of Trustees.

Link to this question

**Will ASSOCADS name our organisation as a partner?**

Only after a written agreement approved by the Board is in place, and with your permission. ASSOCADS does not name, or show the logo of, any organisation it is only talking to.

Link to this question

**Is a partnership the same as organisational membership?**

No. Organisational membership is a category of membership, with an annual fee, that gives an organisation's people access to programmes and benefits. A partnership is a written agreement to work together on something specific, such as a series of workshops or a research project.

Link to this question

**Can a college have an ASSOCADS group on its campus?**

A college or university can propose one through the partnership enquiry. Like every group, a campus group needs the approval of the Board of Trustees.

Link to this question

## Support and donations

**Are donations to ASSOCADS tax-deductible?**

Not at present. ASSOCADS intends to apply for registration under sections 12AB and 80G of the Income Tax Act after the trust is registered. Until 80G approval is granted, donations do not qualify for a tax deduction.

Link to this question

**Can ASSOCADS accept foreign donations?**

No. ASSOCADS cannot accept foreign contributions until it holds registration or prior permission under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010.

Link to this question

**Can I donate to ASSOCADS now?**

ASSOCADS is not yet accepting donations. We will open giving once the trust is registered and its bank account is in place.

Link to this question

**What will donations be used for?**

Only for the objects in the trust deed, such as training, events, research, responsible AI and AI for social good. Trustees are honorary and receive no payment for acting as trustees. If the trust were ever dissolved, its assets would pass to a similar charitable institution, never to trustees or members.

Link to this question

**Is a pledge a commitment to pay?**

No. A pledge tells us what you would like to give once ASSOCADS can accept it. Nothing is paid and no payment details are asked for. We will write to you when giving opens, and you decide then.

Link to this question

**Can my company sponsor an event?**

Sponsorship, like a donation, can be accepted only once giving opens. You can tell us now what you would like to sponsor through the pledge or sponsor form on the Support page, and we will be in touch.

Link to this question

## Website and privacy

**What does ASSOCADS do with the details I send in a form?**

The form is emailed to the ASSOCADS secretariat so that someone can reply, and you receive a short acknowledgement. The website does not keep a copy in a database. The privacy notice explains what each form collects, who processes it and how to ask for it to be corrected or deleted.

Link to this question

**Does this website use cookies?**

No. ASSOCADS sets no cookies and uses no advertising tools. It counts visits and measures page speed with Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights, which work without cookies and show us totals, not who you are. In your browser, until you close the tab, the website remembers only that you closed the notice at the top of the page, and your answers on the membership form until you send it. If you choose a light or dark theme, your browser keeps that choice until you change it. The privacy notice explains each service.

Link to this question

**How do I ask ASSOCADS to correct or delete my data?**

Write to the data protection contact given in the privacy notice. Say what you would like us to do, and use the email address you used on the form, so that we can find your details.

Link to this question

**Is this website accessible?**

ASSOCADS aims to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 at level AA. The accessibility statement says what has been tested, what is known not to work well yet, and how to report a problem.

Link to this question
